regimens.indication: Primary Humoral Immunodeficiency (PI) — Adults and Pediatrics (>= 3 years)

refs.quote: PRIVIGEN is indicated as replacement therapy for primary humoral immunodeficiency (PI).
The recommended dose of PRIVIGEN for patients with PI is 200 to 800 mg/kg (2 to 8 mL/kg), administered every 3 to 4 weeks.

regimens.dose_text: 200 to 800 mg/kg (2 to 8 mL/kg) IV every 3 to 4 weeks, adjusted to achieve desired serum IgG trough levels and clinical response. Initial infusion rate: 0.5 mg/kg/min (0.005 mL/kg/min); may increase as tolerated up to 8 mg/kg/min (0.08 mL/kg/min).

regimens.indication: Primary Humoral Immunodeficiency (PI) — Measles Exposure Prophylaxis

refs.quote: If a patient has been exposed to measles, it may be prudent to administer an extra dose of Immune Globulin Intravenous as soon as possible and within 6 days of exposure. A dose of 400 mg/kg should provide a serum level > 240 mIU/mL of measles antibodies for at least two weeks.

dose.frequency: single extra dose within 6 days of exposure (or >= 530 mg/kg if at risk of future exposure)

regimens.dose_text: 400 mg/kg IV as soon as possible and within 6 days of measles exposure. If at risk of future measles exposure and receiving < 530 mg/kg every 3–4 weeks, increase maintenance dose to at least 530 mg/kg.

regimens.indication: Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP) — Adults and Adolescents (>= 15 years)

refs.quote: PRIVIGEN is indicated for the treatment of patients age 15 years and older with chronic immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) to raise platelet counts.
The recommended dose of PRIVIGEN for patients with chronic ITP is 1 g/kg (10 mL/kg) administered daily for 2 consecutive days, resulting in a total dosage of 2 g/kg.

dose.frequency: once daily for 2 consecutive days (total 2 g/kg)

regimens.dose_text: 1 g/kg (10 mL/kg) IV daily for 2 consecutive days (total 2 g/kg). Initial infusion rate: 0.5 mg/kg/min (0.005 mL/kg/min); may increase as tolerated up to 4 mg/kg/min (0.04 mL/kg/min).

regimens.indication: Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP) — Loading Dose (Adults)

refs.quote: PRIVIGEN is indicated for the treatment of adults with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) to improve neuromuscular disability and impairment.
PRIVIGEN may be initially administered as a total loading dose of 2 g/kg (20 mL/kg) given in divided doses over two to five consecutive days.

dose.frequency: total loading dose in divided doses over 2 to 5 consecutive days

regimens.dose_text: Total loading dose of 2 g/kg (20 mL/kg) IV given in divided doses over 2 to 5 consecutive days. Initial infusion rate: 0.5 mg/kg/min (0.005 mL/kg/min); may gradually increase up to 8 mg/kg/min (0.08 mL/kg/min) as tolerated (use minimum practicable rate if at risk for thrombosis, renal dysfunction, or volume overload).

regimens.indication: Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP) — Maintenance Dose (Adults)

refs.quote: PRIVIGEN may be administered as a maintenance infusion of 1 g/kg (10 mL/kg) administered in a single infusion given in one day or divided into two doses given on two consecutive days, every 3 weeks. Maintenance therapy beyond 6 months has not been studied.

dose.frequency: every 3 weeks (single infusion on 1 day or divided over 2 consecutive days)

regimens.dose_text: 1 g/kg (10 mL/kg) IV every 3 weeks, administered as a single infusion in 1 day or divided into 2 doses on 2 consecutive days. Initial infusion rate: 0.5 mg/kg/min; may gradually increase up to 8 mg/kg/min as tolerated. Maintenance therapy beyond 6 months has not been studied.

value.drug_or_class: Live Attenuated Viral Vaccines (Measles, Mumps, Rubella, Varicella)
value.effect: Passively acquired antiviral antibodies neutralize vaccine viruses, inhibiting protective immune response development for up to 3 to 11 months.
value.management: Defer live virus immunization for at least 3 months following IVIg infusion; revaccinate if administered within 14 days prior to IVIg.

refs.quote: The passive transfer of antibodies with immunoglobulin administration may interfere with the response to live virus vaccines such as measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella

value.drug_or_class: Serological Diagnostic Assays (Coombs Test, Hepatitis, Syphilis Serology)
value.effect: Passive transfer of donor antibodies causes transient positive serologic testing (e.g., direct antiglobulin / Coombs test), mimicking active infection or hemolysis.
value.management: Interpret serological test results with caution and account for recent IVIg administration when evaluating hemolytic or infectious markers.
